// Case study

Northwind Checkout 

A checkout that is ready before the customer has finished reaching for their card.

Visit the live site

Kind

01
The problem

Northwind sells outdoor gear in nine countries, and four in ten carts were abandoned on the payment step. The page waited for three services before it drew anything.

02
The approach
The payment form now renders from the server with the cart already in it; the card fields hydrate on their own.
The whole flow is one state machine, so a slow network can no longer leave the button in two states at once.
Fonts, the logo and the first product image are the only things in the critical path. Everything else waits.
A laptop with a dark dashboard, a phone and a hand reaching in, in an office at dusk
Phone wireframe sketches on paper and a hand with a pen
03
The result

Largest Contentful Paint on a mid-range Android went from 2.9 s to 0.8 s. Completed checkouts rose 11% in the first full month, and support tickets that mention the word stuck fell by two thirds.

We had been tuning the backend for a year. Soren found the two seconds in the browser in his first week.
